newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE IN QUIET TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE IN QUIET TRADE.

text.p: Zimbabwe's money market continued liquid on Friday with short-term rates quoted stable in quiet trade, dealers said.
They said the central Reserve Bank auctioned Z$100 million worth of treasury bills at 16.40 percent which discount houses were re-selling on the secondary market at 16.25 percent.
"Next week about Z$2 billion treasury bills are maturing, so the rate should drop quite significantly," one dealer said.

On Friday, NCDs maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought and sold at 17.25 and 17 percent respectively, unchanged from Thursday and bankers acceptance rates were also quoted stable at 16.60 percent (buying) and 16.35 percent (selling).
Call money was indicated at around 16 percent in a market which closed on Thursday with a Z$131 million surplus.
